tasks.title: Scaffold Ralph as a standalone Python package
tasks.objective: Create Ralph's repo-local Python package skeleton under `ralph/` so later tasks can add behavior without mixing packaging work into runtime modules. Establish the console-script metadata and test-package discovery surface up front.
constraints: Keep Ralph packaged entirely under `ralph/` and independent from `backend/` and Django packaging.
Declare the installed console script as `ralph = "ralph.cli:main"` in `ralph/pyproject.toml`.
Do not add third-party runtime dependencies unless a later task proves one is strictly necessary.
implementation_notes: Create only package metadata and minimal package markers in this task.
Keep `__init__.py` files empty or side-effect free.
Make `ralph/tests` discoverable by `python -m unittest discover -s ralph/tests`.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/pyproject.toml` exists and declares build metadata plus the `ralph` console-script entrypoint.
The listed package directories and `__init__.py` files exist under `ralph/ralph/` and `ralph/tests/`.
Ralph's package metadata does not declare non-build third-party runtime dependencies.
assumptions: The prepared development environment will install Ralph in editable mode before using the `ralph` console script.

tasks.title: Declare typed Ralph failure categories
tasks.objective: Introduce the shared exception surface Ralph uses for deterministic failure reporting. This task should make the spec's named failure categories explicit before configuration, phases, and orchestration start raising errors.
constraints: Define typed failures for feature-folder validation, prompt loading, agent execution, malformed status contract, bookkeeping validation, and retrospective failure.
Keep the error surface repo-local and stdlib-only.
Do not encode CLI exit handling or lifecycle recovery policy in the exception definitions.
implementation_notes: Prefer a small inheritance tree rooted in one Ralph-specific base exception.
Add only failure classes needed to make the spec's explicit categories addressable in later modules.
Keep exception classes free of side effects and file-system logic.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/errors.py` defines Ralph-specific exception types for each explicit failure category named in the spec.
Later modules can import typed Ralph failures from one shared location instead of inventing ad hoc exception names.
The error module contains only exception definitions and related typing helpers.
assumptions: Additional narrow exception subclasses may be added later if they remain children of the shared Ralph error surface.

tasks.title: Implement resolved run config and feature validation
tasks.objective: Implement the typed configuration layer that resolves CLI inputs into validated runtime settings and feature-local paths. This task should make feature-folder validation deterministic before any agent or lifecycle code runs.
constraints: Expose `RunConfig` with the resolved feature directory, max iterations, coding model, retro model, retro-only mode, and selected agent identifier.
Reject absolute feature-directory paths and missing required feature files through typed failures.
Resolve derived paths for `spec.md`, `tasks.json`, `ralph.txt`, `ralph.retro.md`, `.ralph/`, `.ralph/sessions/`, and `.ralph/lock`.
Keep feature-folder validation in `ralph.config` rather than duplicating it in lifecycle modules.
implementation_notes: Default the v1 agent identifier to `codex` without hard-coding Codex logic into lifecycle modules.
Use typed configuration objects instead of raw dictionaries.
Represent retro-only state explicitly even though the public Python CLI will expose `retro` as a subcommand.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/config.py` exposes `RunConfig` plus helpers that derive all Ralph runtime paths from a relative feature directory.
Invalid feature-directory inputs and missing required files fail through typed Ralph errors instead of generic shell exits.
Later modules can read the resolved agent identifier and all derived artifact paths from `RunConfig` without recomputing them.
assumptions: Relative feature paths are resolved from the caller's current working directory at runtime.

tasks.title: Define the shared agent protocol
tasks.objective: Add the shared agent abstraction Ralph lifecycle code will consume in v1. This task creates the typed execution contract without binding any caller to the concrete Codex backend.
constraints: Define `Agent` as the execution protocol for agent backends.
Define `AgentResult` as the structured result of one agent invocation.
Keep the protocol focused on prompt text, model selection, stdout content, exit status, and diagnostics metadata.
implementation_notes: Do not parse Ralph status lines in the agent layer.
Do not encode retry policy or lifecycle state in the agent protocol.
Keep the protocol usable by both coding and retrospective phases.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/agents/base.py` defines `Agent` and `AgentResult` as reusable typed interfaces.
The shared protocol is concrete enough for both fake test agents and the real Codex adapter to implement.
Lifecycle modules can depend on this module without importing any concrete backend.
assumptions: A single synchronous agent invocation contract is sufficient for v1.

tasks.title: Implement the v1 Codex agent adapter
tasks.objective: Implement the concrete `codex` backend Ralph uses in v1 while preserving the shell prototype's external command contract. This task isolates subprocess execution and temp-file handling from lifecycle control flow.
constraints: Implement a concrete agent backend that executes `codex --model <model> --ask-for-approval never -c shell_environment_policy.inherit=all exec --ephemeral --sandbox danger-full-access -o <tempfile> -`.
Capture the temp-file payload, exit status, and subprocess diagnostics, then remove the temp file reliably in success and failure paths.
Use only Python standard-library facilities for subprocess and temp-file handling.
implementation_notes: Keep all Codex-specific flags and subprocess wiring inside this module.
Preserve stderr or subprocess-failure details so later layers can raise typed agent-execution failures.
Do not embed any Ralph status parsing or bookkeeping validation here.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/agents/codex.py` defines the v1 Codex-backed implementation of the shared `Agent` contract.
The adapter executes the documented Codex command flags and returns structured `AgentResult` data from the temp-file payload.
The temp output file is removed after both successful and failing invocations.
assumptions: Future peer adapters may be added later without changing lifecycle-module imports.

tasks.title: Resolve configured agent identifiers
tasks.objective: Add the factory boundary that maps a configured agent identifier to a concrete backend implementation. This task keeps agent selection out of CLI and lifecycle code.
constraints: Expose `resolve_agent(agent_name: str) -> Agent` as the only public agent-resolution entrypoint.
Support the `codex` identifier in v1.
Raise a typed Ralph failure for unknown agent identifiers instead of silently falling back.
implementation_notes: Keep the factory logic small and declarative.
Do not import lifecycle modules here.
Do not add configuration parsing to the factory; it should receive an already resolved agent identifier.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/agents/factory.py` exposes `resolve_agent(agent_name: str) -> Agent`.
Resolving `codex` returns the concrete Codex adapter without callers importing `ralph.agents.codex` directly.
Unknown agent identifiers fail deterministically through a typed Ralph error.
assumptions: The factory may remain a simple name-to-class mapping in v1.

tasks.title: Persist run sessions and current-session pointers
tasks.objective: Implement the machine-readable session store Ralph needs for auditability and resume support. This task owns feature-local `.ralph/` creation, per-session records, and `current.json` pointer semantics.
constraints: Create `.ralph/` on first use and persist per-run records in `.ralph/sessions/<session-id>.json`.
Maintain `.ralph/sessions/current.json` as the pointer to the current incomplete session when one exists, or otherwise the latest terminal session.
Store only control-plane data such as resolved config, current phase, iteration count, last phase outcome, timestamps, agent result metadata, and overall run outcome.
Limit terminal outcomes in v1 to `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, `max_iterations`, and `degraded`.
implementation_notes: Keep session identifiers filesystem-safe and unique within a feature folder.
Do not duplicate `ralph.txt` narrative text or persist full prompt and response bodies.
Expose explicit read and write operations for session creation, update, and finalization.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/session.py` can create `.ralph/`, persist per-session JSON records, and update `.ralph/sessions/current.json` with the documented pointer behavior.
Session records contain only control-plane metadata and the documented v1 terminal-outcome vocabulary.
Later lifecycle code can load the current incomplete session or latest terminal session without recomputing file paths.
assumptions: Session identifiers may be implementation-defined as long as they are unique and stable for file lookup.

tasks.title: Implement lock ownership and stale-lock inspection
tasks.objective: Add the active-run locking behavior Ralph needs for one-active-run-per-feature enforcement. This task implements `.ralph/lock` persistence, heartbeat support, and stale-lock inspection without deciding when to reclaim locks.
constraints: Persist `.ralph/lock` with at least session id, pid, hostname, started-at timestamp, and last-heartbeat timestamp.
Expose heartbeat refresh operations so the orchestrator can update lock state at phase boundaries.
Treat a lock as stale only when the recorded process is not running on the recorded host and the last heartbeat is older than 10 minutes.
Do not auto-reclaim locks in the session layer.
implementation_notes: Provide explicit APIs for lock acquire, release, heartbeat refresh, and stale-state inspection.
Keep hostname and process-liveness checks conservative and deterministic.
Separate lock-state reporting from run-versus-resume policy.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/session.py` can persist and load a structured lock record with the documented fields.
The session module can distinguish active, stale, and absent lock states using the host and heartbeat rules from the spec.
Lock acquisition, release, and heartbeat refresh are available as explicit operations for lifecycle code.
assumptions: A conservative local-process liveness check is sufficient as long as cross-host locks are never reclaimed without the recorded-host rule passing.

tasks.title: Define shared lifecycle phase contracts
tasks.objective: Create the shared phase boundary the orchestrator and phase packages will use. Each phase must remain a single-shot unit that returns a local outcome without embedding global workflow policy.
constraints: Define `Phase` as the shared phase contract.
Define `PhaseOutcome` with the exact values `next_iteration`, `completed`, `blocked`, and `failed`.
Define `PhaseResult` as the structured result of a single phase invocation.
The phase contract must not encode which phase comes next.
implementation_notes: Keep the base types free of prompt loading, session persistence, and subprocess execution logic.
Use explicit typed values for phase outcomes so malformed states cannot be expressed casually.
Design the result shape so the orchestrator can record metadata without depending on raw backend internals.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/base.py` exposes `Phase`, `PhaseOutcome`, and `PhaseResult` with the documented v1 names and outcome values.
The shared phase contract is single-shot and phase-local rather than loop-aware.
Both the code and retro phase packages can depend on this module without importing each other.
assumptions: A small enum or equivalent typed vocabulary is sufficient for v1 phase outcomes.

tasks.title: Move the coding prompt into the code phase package
tasks.objective: Create the code phase's own prompt asset and prompt-rendering helper. This task should make the coding prompt phase-local before any status parsing or bookkeeping validation is added.
constraints: Keep prompt ownership inside `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/code/` and do not introduce a centralized prompt module.
Preserve the prompt as a Markdown file on disk.
Replace the `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder with the resolved feature-directory path before agent execution.
implementation_notes: Carry forward the existing coding prompt contract from `ralph/prompts/code.md` without broadening Ralph's user-facing behavior.
Limit this task to prompt asset placement and rendering support.
Do not parse agent output or validate bookkeeping in this task.
acceptance_criteria: The code phase package contains its own `prompt.md` asset and a helper that renders it for one feature directory.
Rendering the prompt substitutes the resolved feature-directory path for the `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder.
No shared `ralph.lifecycle.prompts` module is introduced.
assumptions: The old `ralph/prompts/code.md` file may remain temporarily until the compatibility shim stops relying on it.

tasks.title: Parse coding status lines into typed outcomes
tasks.objective: Implement the strict first-line response parser the coding phase uses to turn model output into typed control signals. This task should formalize the shell script's implicit status contract.
constraints: Accept only the exact first-line values `RALPH_STATUS=CONTINUE`, `RALPH_STATUS=COMPLETE`, and `RALPH_STATUS=BLOCKED`.
Treat a missing first line, malformed status value, or `RALPH_STATUS=BLOCKED` response without the required human-readable blocker line as a typed contract violation.
Keep status parsing phase-local instead of moving it into the agent layer or orchestrator.
implementation_notes: Return typed results that the code phase can map directly into `PhaseOutcome` values.
Strip carriage returns consistently before comparing the first line.
Do not inspect `tasks.json` in this parser; bookkeeping validation belongs in a separate task.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/code/status.py` maps the exact Ralph status lines into typed phase-local results.
Malformed status output fails deterministically through a typed Ralph error instead of warning and continuing.
`RALPH_STATUS=BLOCKED` parsing requires a natural-language blocker line in line 2.
assumptions: The parser may preserve the remaining response body for later diagnostics without changing its phase-local responsibility.

tasks.title: Validate coding-phase bookkeeping artifacts
tasks.objective: Implement the narrow, objective bookkeeping validation Ralph performs after each successful coding iteration. This task should enforce only the explicit v1 artifact contract and nothing broader.
constraints: Validate only these rules: `tasks.json` exists and is parseable, `ralph.txt` exists or was created, `RALPH_STATUS=BLOCKED` includes the required blocker line, `RALPH_STATUS=COMPLETE` is accepted only when every task entry has `status: "completed"`, and `RALPH_STATUS=CONTINUE` is accepted only when at least one task entry remains not `completed`.
Do not rewrite `tasks.json` or `ralph.txt` in the harness.
Do not infer implementation correctness from `spec.md`, git state, or ad hoc dependency reasoning.
implementation_notes: Keep bookkeeping validation phase-local because it depends on the coding-phase contract.
Treat parse failures and contract mismatches as typed bookkeeping-validation failures.
If `ralph.txt` is created implicitly, limit the mutation to creating the required bookkeeping artifact.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/code/validation.py` enforces only the documented v1 bookkeeping rules.
`RALPH_STATUS=COMPLETE` is rejected when any task entry in `tasks.json` is not `completed`.
`RALPH_STATUS=CONTINUE` is rejected when every task entry is already `completed`.
assumptions: Task entries in `tasks.json` may omit `status` until they are completed; the bookkeeping validator treats missing or non-`completed` values as pending.

tasks.title: Implement one-shot coding phase execution
tasks.objective: Build the coding phase as a self-contained package that renders its prompt, invokes the abstract agent once, parses the first-line control signal, and validates bookkeeping for that single pass. This task should return a local phase result without deciding whether Ralph repeats the phase or advances to retro.
constraints: Use only the abstract `Agent` interface and shared phase types inside the coding phase.
Perform exactly one prompt render, one agent invocation, one status parse, and one bookkeeping validation per call.
Do not encode iteration loops, next-phase selection, or stale-lock policy in this module.
implementation_notes: Compose the prompt, status parser, and bookkeeping validator from earlier tasks instead of duplicating their logic.
Capture agent-result metadata needed by the orchestrator to persist session state.
Map phase-local status results onto the shared `PhaseOutcome` values.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/code/phase.py` can execute one coding pass and return a `PhaseResult` with typed outcome data.
The coding phase talks only to the shared `Agent` contract and not directly to `CodexAgent`.
The module does not contain loop control or retrospective-transition logic.
assumptions: The code phase may record minimal diagnostics metadata in its `PhaseResult` as long as it does not duplicate full prompt or response bodies.

tasks.title: Move the retro prompt and prerequisites into the retro package
tasks.objective: Create the retrospective phase's own prompt asset and validation helpers. This task should establish phase-local prompt ownership and the retro-only prerequisite rules before the retro phase itself is wired.
constraints: Keep prompt ownership and prompt-related helpers inside `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/retro/`.
Validate that retrospective execution still requires `ralph.txt`.
Keep retrospective rerun mutations limited to retrospective-owned outputs such as `ralph.retro.md`.
implementation_notes: Carry forward the existing retro prompt contract from `ralph/prompts/retro.md` without broadening the feature-folder interface.
Use phase-local helpers for prompt loading and prerequisite checks.
Do not add cross-phase validation helpers here.
acceptance_criteria: The retro phase package contains its own `prompt.md` asset plus helpers for prompt rendering and retro prerequisites.
Retrospective execution fails deterministically when `ralph.txt` is missing.
No centralized lifecycle-validation module is introduced for retro-specific checks.
assumptions: The old `ralph/prompts/retro.md` file may remain temporarily until the compatibility shim no longer relies on it.

tasks.title: Implement one-shot retrospective phase execution
tasks.objective: Build the retrospective phase as a self-contained package that renders its prompt, validates prerequisites, invokes the abstract agent once, and returns a local phase result. This task should keep retrospective behavior phase-local and single-shot.
constraints: Use only the abstract `Agent` interface and shared phase types inside the retro phase.
Perform exactly one prompt render, one agent invocation, and one retro-phase validation per call.
Do not encode coding-loop control, stale-lock policy, or next-phase selection in this module.
implementation_notes: Compose the retro prompt and validation helpers from earlier tasks instead of duplicating them.
Return enough metadata for the orchestrator to distinguish a successful retro pass from a retrospective failure.
Keep retro-phase mutations limited to its owned retrospective output path.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/phases/retro/phase.py` can execute one retrospective pass and return a `PhaseResult` with typed outcome data.
The retro phase depends only on the shared `Agent` contract and not directly on `CodexAgent`.
The module does not write or validate non-retrospective product artifacts.
assumptions: A retrospective pass may return failure diagnostics without persisting full agent response bodies.

tasks.title: Implement the new-session run lifecycle
tasks.objective: Implement the orchestrator logic for starting a fresh Ralph run, enforcing one-active-run-per-feature on the `run` path, iterating the coding phase, and invoking retrospective automatically after code completion. This task should own static phase sequencing and overall outcomes for newly created sessions.
constraints: `run` must validate configuration, create a new session, acquire the lock, refresh heartbeat at phase boundaries, and stop only on `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, `max_iterations`, or `degraded`.
`run` must fail fast when `.ralph/sessions/current.json` points to an incomplete session or `.ralph/lock` is active, and it must tell the operator to use `resume`.
When the code phase reports completion, the orchestrator must run the retrospective phase automatically.
If implementation succeeds and retrospective fails, record the overall run outcome as `degraded` rather than `failed`.
implementation_notes: Keep the v1 phase pipeline static and explicit inside the orchestrator.
Record session progress after each phase boundary using the session store instead of recomputing state from artifacts.
Do not implement stale-lock reclamation or resume behavior in this task.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/orchestrator.py` exposes a `run` path that creates a new session and drives the code phase one iteration at a time.
`run` refuses to continue an existing incomplete session and directs the operator to `resume` instead.
A successful code-phase completion triggers retrospective automatically, and retrospective failure after successful implementation produces a `degraded` run outcome.
assumptions: The orchestrator may expose separate callable entrypoints for `run`, `resume`, and `retro` as long as `run` owns the new-session policy.

tasks.title: Implement resume semantics and stale-lock recovery
tasks.objective: Extend the orchestrator with the exact `resume` behavior the spec requires. This task should make session continuation deterministic, restrict stale-lock reclamation to `resume`, and explicitly reject terminal sessions.
constraints: `resume` must load exactly one existing incomplete session and continue it without creating a new session.
Only `resume` may reclaim a stale lock automatically under the documented host, process, and 10-minute heartbeat rules.
Terminal sessions with outcomes `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, `max_iterations`, and `degraded` are closed and may not be resumed.
If no incomplete session exists, `resume` must fail through a typed Ralph error instead of starting over.
implementation_notes: Reuse the session store and lock inspection APIs from earlier tasks instead of reimplementing stale-state checks.
Continue iteration counting and session timestamps from the persisted session record.
Keep terminal-session rejection explicit in code and acceptance criteria rather than implying it through assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/lifecycle/orchestrator.py` exposes a `resume` path that continues exactly one incomplete persisted session.
`resume` may reclaim a stale lock only when the session layer reports the stale-lock rule is satisfied.
`resume` rejects terminal sessions with outcomes `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, `max_iterations`, and `degraded` instead of reopening them.
assumptions: The current-session pointer identifies the session `resume` should attempt first when one incomplete session exists.

tasks.title: Implement CLI subcommands and typed command dispatch
tasks.objective: Build the public Python CLI surface Ralph exposes in v1. This task should wire `run`, `resume`, and `retro` to the resolved agent and lifecycle entrypoints without adding an `inspect` command.
constraints: Expose public subcommands `run`, `resume`, and `retro` through the installed `ralph` console script.
Do not add a public `inspect` command in v1.
Resolve the configured agent through `ralph.agents.factory` before calling lifecycle entrypoints.
Map typed Ralph failures to deterministic non-zero CLI exits and operator-facing error messages.
implementation_notes: Use one argument-parsing surface for all public Python CLI commands.
Keep shell-compatibility flag translation out of this module; that belongs in `ralph/ralph.sh`.
Make the `retro` command use the same config and agent-resolution flow as the other public commands.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph/cli.py` defines the public Python CLI with `run`, `resume`, and `retro` subcommands and no `inspect` subcommand.
The CLI resolves the configured agent through the factory before delegating to lifecycle entrypoints.
Typed Ralph failures produce deterministic non-zero exits with one operator-facing error message rather than raw tracebacks by default.
assumptions: The CLI may use `argparse` and return integer exit codes from `main()`.

tasks.title: Delegate legacy shell flags to the Python CLI
tasks.objective: Rewrite `ralph/ralph.sh` as a compatibility shim that preserves the old operator interface while delegating all authoritative behavior into Python. This task should keep Bash limited to argument translation and process delegation.
constraints: Preserve the legacy flags `--feature-dir`, `--max-iterations`, `--coding-model`, `--retro-model`, and `--retro-only`.
Map the legacy full-lifecycle flag set to the Python `run` command and map `--retro-only` to the Python `retro` command.
Do not reimplement feature validation, prompt loading, status parsing, or orchestration logic in Bash.
implementation_notes: Keep the shim's responsibility to minimal flag parsing and argument pass-through.
Retain `./ralph/ralph.sh --help` as the legacy operator-facing entrypoint.
Prefer `exec`-style delegation so the Python CLI remains the authoritative process.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/ralph.sh` still accepts the legacy flag set and delegates execution into the Python CLI.
`--retro-only` routes to the Python retrospective workflow instead of a Bash-owned implementation path.
The shell wrapper no longer contains the old coding loop, status switch, or direct Codex invocation.
assumptions: The compatibility shim may keep a legacy-style usage message as long as the delegated behavior remains authoritative in Python.

tasks.title: Add fake-agent support for deterministic Ralph tests
tasks.objective: Create reusable fake-agent test support so Ralph's deterministic test suite can exercise lifecycle behavior without requiring a real `codex` binary or network access. This task should provide the test doubles other validation tasks depend on.
constraints: Implement fake-agent helpers against the shared `Agent` contract from `ralph.agents.base`.
Keep test helpers deterministic and stdlib-only.
Do not make fake-agent behavior depend on the real `codex` binary.
implementation_notes: Provide small helpers for scripted agent outputs and controlled failures.
Keep test-only utilities inside `ralph/tests/` rather than production modules.
Model only behavior needed by the deterministic Ralph tests.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/tests/fakes.py` provides reusable fake-agent support for deterministic unit and integration tests.
The fake-agent helpers implement the shared `Agent` contract closely enough to exercise orchestration logic.
The test helpers do not invoke external binaries or networked services.
assumptions: A scripted sequence of `AgentResult` values and failures is sufficient to drive the required tests.

tasks.title: Add deterministic unit tests for config and phase helpers
tasks.objective: Add focused deterministic tests for the local module contracts Ralph depends on before end-to-end orchestration. This task should cover the spec's helper-level failure cases without using the real Codex adapter.
constraints: Cover deterministic failures for malformed first-line status, bookkeeping validation failure, and missing `ralph.txt` in retrospective mode.
Keep these tests independent from the real `codex` binary.
Use the standard `unittest` runner so `python -m unittest discover -s ralph/tests` remains the canonical direct test command.
implementation_notes: Test configuration resolution and feature-path validation directly through `RunConfig` helpers.
Exercise session-store and lock-state helpers through temporary feature directories.
Keep helper-level tests focused on one contract per test case instead of reproducing full lifecycle runs.
acceptance_criteria: The added unit tests cover malformed coding status parsing, bookkeeping validation failure, and missing `ralph.txt` in retrospective mode.
Session and config tests exercise the persisted-path and lock-state helpers without calling the real agent adapter.
`python -m unittest discover -s ralph/tests` can discover the added test modules.
assumptions: Temporary directories created within the test process are sufficient to simulate feature folders for helper-level tests.

tasks.title: Add lifecycle integration tests for run and resume
tasks.objective: Add deterministic integration tests that exercise Ralph's session lifecycle, loop control, and degraded-success behavior through the orchestrator. This task should cover the spec's end-to-end lifecycle scenarios with fake agents.
constraints: Cover successful multi-iteration completion, blocked run, resume after an interrupted run, run failure when an incomplete session already exists, stale-lock recovery through `resume`, and degraded success when retrospective fails after implementation completes.
Use fake agents and temporary feature directories rather than the real Codex adapter.
Keep the tests deterministic and compatible with `python -m unittest discover -s ralph/tests`.
implementation_notes: Model interrupted runs by persisting session state and lock artifacts, then invoking the orchestrator resume path.
Verify persisted session outcomes and lock behavior directly from the feature-local `.ralph/` artifacts.
Keep run-path and resume-path coverage in separate test modules so the scenarios stay bounded.
acceptance_criteria: The added integration tests cover the exact lifecycle scenarios named in the spec for `run`, `resume`, stale locks, and degraded retrospective failure.
The tests verify that `run` refuses an existing incomplete session and that `resume` rejects terminal sessions.
The integration suite runs without a real `codex` binary or network access.
assumptions: CLI-level behavior may be verified indirectly through orchestrator entrypoints as long as the lifecycle scenarios remain fully covered.

tasks.title: Add repo-root Make targets for Ralph verification
tasks.objective: Expose Ralph's stable repository task surface through the root `Makefile`. This task should make Ralph test and verification entrypoints discoverable alongside the rest of the repo workflow.
constraints: Add at least `ralph-test` and `ralph-verify` to the root `Makefile` and `make help` output.
`ralph-test` must run Ralph's deterministic test suite.
`ralph-verify` must run Ralph's tests plus any Ralph-specific lint or typecheck commands actually introduced by this plan.
Do not invent a new non-stdlib lint or typecheck toolchain solely to satisfy this target.
implementation_notes: Keep Ralph targets repo-root entrypoints rather than backend-specific wrappers.
Use direct commands that operate from the repository root and target the `ralph/` package explicitly.
If no Ralph-specific lint or typecheck command exists by the end of implementation, keep `ralph-verify` limited to the commands that do exist.
acceptance_criteria: `make help` lists `ralph-test` and `ralph-verify`.
`ralph-test` invokes the deterministic Ralph test suite under `ralph/tests/`.
`ralph-verify` runs `ralph-test` plus any Ralph-specific verification commands that were actually introduced.
assumptions: The Ralph package remains small enough that repo-root Make targets can invoke its verification commands directly.

tasks.title: Document the Python CLI and recovery model
tasks.objective: Update Ralph's operator documentation to describe the Python CLI, the compatibility shim, and the feature-local recovery artifacts. This task should document the new behavior without changing the implementation plan's scope.
constraints: Document the installed `ralph` console script with `run`, `resume`, and `retro`.
Document `./ralph/ralph.sh` as a compatibility shim that preserves the legacy interface.

Document `.ralph/` session artifacts, stale-lock recovery through `resume`, degraded outcomes, retrospective rerun behavior, and the explicit corrupted-state fallback of deleting `.ralph/` intentionally before starting fresh.
implementation_notes: Keep Ralph documented as a repo-local harness rather than a backend subsystem or hosted service.
Describe the one-time editable-install assumption for the public Python CLI.
Do not rewrite repository-wide workflow docs; keep the changes local to `ralph/README.md`.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/README.md` documents install plus the public `run`, `resume`, and `retro` subcommands.
The README explains how the compatibility shim maps legacy usage to the Python CLI.
The README explicitly describes `.ralph/` artifacts, stale-lock recovery, degraded runs, retro rerun behavior, and the manual corrupted-state fallback.
assumptions: Ralph-specific operator documentation belongs in `ralph/README.md` rather than the repo root.

tasks.title: Execute the Ralph verification command matrix
tasks.objective: Run the final repo-local verification commands that prove the new harness surface works in the prepared development environment. This task should confirm the deterministic path and keep the live Codex smoke path optional.
constraints: Run `python -m pip install -e ralph`, `python -m unittest discover -s ralph/tests`, `make ralph-test`, `make ralph-verify`, and `./ralph/ralph.sh --help`.
Treat a real `ralph run --feature-dir ...` smoke execution as optional and do not require a live `codex` binary for this task to pass.
Do not modify product code while performing this validation task.
implementation_notes: Run the verification commands from the repository root.
Record failures as verification evidence and fix them through the implementation tasks they point to rather than weakening acceptance criteria.
If the optional real-Codex smoke path is skipped, leave the deterministic command matrix as the required evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The deterministic verification commands complete successfully in the prepared development environment.
